QF.id: III-C Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices_23

question.text: In the Supreme Court order regarding front-running, which of the following was identified as a form of front-running?

answer.text: All three: self-front-running (hedging through futures or options against own block trades); tippee trading (trading by third parties tipped on impending block trades); and trading ahead (intermediary trading before customer block orders for own profit)
Self-front-running - hedging through futures or options against own block trades
Tippee trading - trading by third parties tipped on impending block trades
Trading ahead - intermediary trading before customer block orders for own profit

explanation.text: The Logic: As per Case 8.2 in the workbook, the Supreme Court identified three forms of front-running: (i) tippee trading — trading by third parties tipped about impending block trades; (ii) self-front-running — hedging via futures or options against one's own block trades; and (iii) trading ahead — an intermediary trading before a customer's block order to capture price impact. All three are recognised forms. The Trap: Candidates may think front-running only refers to an intermediary trading ahead of a customer order. The Supreme Court order recognises a wider set, including tipping third parties and self-hedging via derivatives against one's own block trades, so a single-form answer is incomplete. Note: Front-running is broader than just an intermediary trading ahead of a client — tipping third parties and self-hedging through derivatives against one's own block trades are equally caught.
